title: POC Weekly Caching Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync to review KV/prefix cache hit rates, discuss prompt reuse strategy, and agree next steps for TTL tuning and benchmark runs. Customer sees improvement but hit rate still below target for long-tail prompts; SE recommends hybrid prefix + KV approach and a short benchmark of 50k requests on Dedicated staging. Action items assigned.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-15 10:00 UTC | Duration 45m | Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Chen, Carlos Ruiz, Priya Nair (FinSolve)

Summary (auto): quick results review; hit rates up ~12% after ruleset change; still gap for long-tail prompts; discussed canonical prompt templates and micro-prefixing; plan to run 50k request benchmark on staging Dedicated nodes; send security docs and pricing uplift for Dedicated pilot.

00:00:00 Jordan Lee: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll get started in a minute, uh feel free to drop notes in the chat
00:00:08 Maya Chen: yeah thanks Jordan, morning all
00:00:12 Samir Patel: morning Maya, Carlos, Priya. quick agenda: we go through last week's numbers, hit rates, then tuning recs, and then next steps.
00:00:22 Carlos Ruiz: sounds good, let's do it
00:01:05 Jordan Lee: ok Samir you wanna kick off with the hit-rate slide?
00:01:10 Samir Patel: sure — so per the dashboard we pushed the conservative ruleset last week, overall KV hit rate moved from 8% to about 20% for the top 5 intents, prefix cache shows 32% for short templates. but long-tail prompts still mostly cold — those are the dynamic trade negotiation prompts, long user contexts.
00:01:35 Priya Nair: when you say prefix cache 32% is that per-token or per-request? I want to make sure we're comparing apples
00:01:40 Samir Patel: good question — that's per-request level, so 32% of incoming requests matched a prefix hash and returned a cached KV snapshot. per-token hit is slightly higher because of prefix continuation, but we reported request-level.
00:02:05 Maya Chen: ok that's promising but our SLO needs 60% effective reuse to hit cost targets for production — is that realistic?
00:02:12 Samir Patel: it's aggressive for your current prompt variability. recommendation: standardize 6 canonical prompt templates for the negotiation flows + apply micro-prefixing on the session metadata. That should push top intents to 50-60%.
00:02:28 Carlos Ruiz: quick clarification — micro-prefixing is the short static header only right? we don't want to cache user PII obviously
00:02:34 Samir Patel: exact — just the normalized system and instruction blocks, strip user identifiers, and then hash; Redwood's KV cache supports prefix normalization hooks in the runtime.
00:03:12 Priya Nair: is that something we can enable without redeploying? we are on the hosted trial but moving to Dedicated staging next week
00:03:20 Jordan Lee: you can toggle normalization rules via the config--for Dedicated it'll be a config flag on the deployment; for hosted we can push a runtime config change for your account. No code change needed.
00:04:05 Samir Patel: performance notes: enabling prefix normalization increases hit rate but may add ~2-4ms of preprocessing per request on average; on Dedicated that's negligible but for hosted we saw a small P95 uptick.
00:04:34 Maya Chen: acceptable if cost reduces. also how are you evicting KV entries — LRU? Our worry is stale context for long-running sessions
00:04:43 Samir Patel: eviction defaults to adaptive TTL + LRU; for sessions we recommend session-scoped short TTLs (5-10 minutes) and promote popular prefixes to a pinned tier. that addresses staleness.
00:05:30 Carlos Ruiz: How often do you recompute the KV hash? if user edits earlier messages that would change the KV and cause misses
00:05:38 Samir Patel: KV is computed at request time based on the normalized prefix; if upstream edits occur the hash changes and you get a miss — we suggest storing a lightweight session summary token to reduce churn.
00:06:12 Priya Nair: we ran a small internal sim of 5k requests and saw only 18% KV hit, your numbers show 20% — close enough. the big gap is the tail where the negotiation context changes a lot.
00:06:38 Jordan Lee: thanks Priya. Samir, any tuning recs specifically for the tail?
00:06:44 Samir Patel: yes — two prong: 1) canonicalize prompts and extract stable context keys (e.g., user role, product category) to include in prefix; 2) enable hybrid strategy: prefix cache for templates + short-lived KV entries for session-specific heavy tokens. hybrid gives best coverage.
00:07:20 Maya Chen: ok what's the risk of over-canonicalizing and losing nuance? some prompts need exact slots to be preserved
00:07:28 Samir Patel: balance — only canonicalize system/instruction and predictable metadata; keep variable slots in the fresh request. Also add a guardrail: evaluation set that checks generation quality drift after any caching rule change.
00:07:52 Carlos Ruiz: gotta keep the QA step — can't have business logic break. who runs that eval?
00:07:56 Jordan Lee: Redwood can run baseline evals and we can provide the harness; or you can run it locally — we can share the eval script and sample prompts.
00:08:15 Maya Chen: share the harness please. we'll run the regression tests on staging Dedicated before we flip caching on prod.
00:08:22 Samir Patel: noted.
00:08:40 Samir Patel: now on metrics — we've instrumented per-route hit rate and token-level saving. for your negotiation route, estimated cost reduction at 50% reuse is ~38% per-token cost. current projected uplift to Dedicated pricing tier reduces that further.
00:09:12 Priya Nair: question on Dedicated — will we be able to pin quantization profiles? we need INT8 for some models
00:09:18 Jordan Lee: yes Dedicated supports quantized variants and you can pin a model + quant profile. we'll include that in the Dedicated config sheet.
00:09:45 Maya Chen: ok good. next: TTL and eviction tuning — what are recommended defaults for our load pattern?
00:09:52 Samir Patel: start with request-level TTL 30s, session TTL 5 min for KV entries, and a pinned list for high-frequency templates with TTL 1h. then iterate based on hit-rate telemetry.
00:10:30 Carlos Ruiz: telemetry — is that in Redwood Console? can we get per-team dashboards and retention to 90 days?
00:10:37 Jordan Lee: yes Redwood Console has per-route dashboards; retention 90 days is an enterprise add-on but we can enable a 30-day default and extend via the contract.
00:11:05 Maya Chen: security question: where are cached KV blobs stored and are they encrypted at rest? need SOC2 proof for encryption and KMS integration for Dedicated
00:11:15 Samir Patel: KV snapshots are stored encrypted at rest; Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. I'll send you the security whitepaper and SOC2 excerpts.
00:11:38 Priya Nair: can we scrub user PII before caching?
00:11:42 Samir Patel: yes — normalization hooks can mask or drop PII fields before hash. we have common scrub rules we can share.
00:12:10 Maya Chen: great.
00:12:33 Jordan Lee: ok moving to the benchmark plan — we propose a 50k request run on your Dedicated staging with canonicalized prompts to validate hit rates and latency. Samir?
00:12:43 Samir Patel: process: we'll coordinate with Carlos to spin staging Dedicated for 24 hours, run the 50k synthetic mix (we provide generator), measure KV/prefix hit, per-token latency P50/P95, and quality regressions via the eval harness. Estimate time: run plus analysis 2-3 days.
00:13:05 Carlos Ruiz: timeline works, we'll provision staging Friday. who owns running the generator?
00:13:12 Samir Patel: Redwood runs it if you grant access; or you run it with our script. I'd prefer we run the first pass to control variables.
00:13:21 Maya Chen: fine, Redwood run first pass.
00:13:25 Priya Nair: what's the expected hit rate after canonicalization + micro-prefixing?
00:13:30 Samir Patel: for top flows 50-60%, overall maybe 35-40% across the mix, because the tail remains. but cost savings still meaningful.
00:13:52 Jordan Lee: pricing note: moving to Dedicated staging has a modest uplift in monthly minimums; I'll send a quote.
00:14:05 Maya Chen: send to my procurement alias please.
00:14:10 Jordan Lee: will do.
00:14:25 Carlos Ruiz: quick note — our infra folks want to ensure network egress is within our VPC for data residency, is that supported on Dedicated?
00:14:33 Jordan Lee: yes Dedicated can be deployed in your VPC with private networking and no egress to public internet for inference traffic. we'll include the VPC diagram in the docs.
00:14:55 Priya Nair: can you also include audit logs retention options?
00:14:59 Samir Patel: yes audit logs, RBAC, SSO all supported — will send details.
00:15:18 Maya Chen: ok great.
00:15:50 Jordan Lee: let's capture action items — I'll read them and then we can add any others.
00:15:55 Jordan Lee: Action item 1: Samir to share canonical prompt templates and normalization hook examples.
00:16:05 Samir Patel: Action item 2: Redwood to run 50k synthetic benchmark on Dedicated staging, coordinate with Carlos, target run next week.
00:16:15 Carlos Ruiz: Action item 3: FinSolve to provide a 1k sample of anonymized real prompts for eval harness.
00:16:28 Priya Nair: Action item 4: Maya to confirm procurement alias and required POC paperwork.
00:16:40 Jordan Lee: Action item 5: Jordan to send Dedicated pricing sheet and security whitepaper (SOC2/KMS).
00:16:50 Maya Chen: all noted
00:17:05 Samir Patel: a few quick technical clarifications — when we run the benchmark we'll capture per-route token savings, KV miss reasons (edit churn, normalization mismatch), and we can output a CSV for your team.
00:17:25 Carlos Ruiz: good, that will help debug the tail.
00:17:55 Priya Nair: any blockers for enabling micro-prefixing now on hosted?
00:18:01 Samir Patel: none, if you want to try on hosted we can enable the normalization rules for your account later today — but recommend running the eval first to check quality.
00:18:20 Maya Chen: let's hold on hosted — we'll wait for Dedicated benchmark then decide.
00:18:28 Jordan Lee: ok noted.
00:19:05 Samir Patel: quick FYI — we saw one weird edge case where template variation included timestamps, causing misses; we recommend stripping any free-form timestamps in normalization.
00:19:18 Priya Nair: yep saw that in our sim, good callout.
00:19:40 Jordan Lee: anything else from the customer side?
00:19:45 Maya Chen: not from me.
00:19:48 Carlos Ruiz: nothing else.
00:19:52 Priya Nair: no.
00:20:00 Jordan Lee: cool, recap next steps and timeline then
00:20:05 Jordan Lee: Redwood to run benchmark next week (50k) and share results within 3 days of run; Samir to share templates + normalization examples by EOD tomorrow; FinSolve to share 1k anonymized prompts by Thursday; Jordan to send pricing + security docs today.
00:20:26 Maya Chen: ok thanks, that works.
00:20:32 Jordan Lee: perfect, thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and slack.
00:20:38 meeting_end: 00:20:38 (note: meeting recorded until 00:45 per system)

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., micro-prefixing sometimes called micro-pushing in earlier auto-captions). References: "Dedicated" sometimes transcribed as "dedi-cated"; ensure security.doc link in follow-up.
